title: Decide how each result appears - settled, conditional or withheld: a pure decision module in new files that nothing calls yet; it computes no zoning number (work order Part 0, sections 0, 5, 6 and 10; D-090 R229, R237, R238, R240, R255, R257, R258, R267, R268, R269)
objective: Build the part of the engine work that DECIDES HOW EACH RESULT APPEARS, as a pure, deterministic module in NEW files that nothing calls yet (docs/plans/R6B_RESULTS_CONNECTION_WORK_ORDER_2026-10-06.md, Part 0; the first of two engine pieces, built one after the other; this one changes no present behaviour). Given what is known about a lot, the module returns, for each result, one of the three ways of the work order's section 0: settled; conditional, with every condition named (its kind, the assumption in words, what would settle it); or withheld, with the reason, the kind of gap and what would resolve it. It computes NO zoning number: the numbers stay where the engine computes them today. Its output for a value mirrors the merged contract 1.3.0 (`value_state` of packages/contracts/schemas/v1/results.schema.json: way, conditions[kind, assumption, settled_by], or label, reason, gap_kind, resolved_by, zr_sections), and a test validates every way object the module can return against the bundled schema. THE RESULTS IT DECIDES: every value key the engine emits today (floor area allowance: max_residential_far, max_residential_floor_area and their two qualifying keys; permitted envelope: min_base_height, max_base_height, max_building_height and their three qualifying keys, max_lot_coverage; building option: achieved_zoning_floor_area, building_floors, building_height, floor_plate_area) and four results that are not value keys today: the rear yard, the setback above the base, the legal unit limit for standard residences, and the legal unit limits for qualifying affordable and for qualifying senior housing. Where every value of an answer is withheld the module says that the whole answer is not available, with its reason, kind and what would resolve it (the contract cannot keep an answer 'available' with no shown value). THE INPUTS, each of which may be 'not given' or 'not read' and is never filled by a default: the district; the lot type; the housing kind chosen (a design choice); the recorded lot area and whether the tax-map outline's area agrees with it (agrees, disagrees, or could not be compared), with both figures for the wording; the lot-reach measurements (services/api/app/spatial/lot_reach.py: from each street line and from the corner point, and the angle; each a value or unknown); the recorded conditions, each 'not read', 'recorded as absent' or 'recorded as present': a special purpose district, a lot split by a district line, a commercial overlay (with its code), an inclusionary housing area, a flood zone, a landmark or historic district; the four conditions that have no data source (waterfront rules, airport height limits, transit easements, a lot close to a district line), each 'not checked', 'checked and absent' or 'recorded as present'; what is known about a special density area ('not given', evidence that the lot is not in one, evidence that it is, or only a user's statement that it is not). The module defines its own input records; it does not import or change the engine's present input object. THE RULES come from the work order: section 0 (the three ways; 'not checked' is never 'confirmed'), section 5 (gaps K1 to K20: the column 'How the result appears in this milestone' and the kinds defined at the head of that section), section 6 (the two lot-area figures) and section 10. The builder writes them out as one decision table in its report, one line per gap and affected result, each line quoting the sentence of the work order it comes from. THE ORCHESTRATOR'S READINGS of points the work order's words leave open (each is the orchestrator's reading, said so in the code and the report, and to be confirmed or corrected by the reviewers): (O1) the contract has two kinds of gap and the work order four: 'information' is missing information; 'owed' and 'question' (which the work order itself calls owed research) are work owed; 'evidence' is missing information when the recorded fact was not read, and work owed when a recorded condition is one the program cannot yet handle; a gap marked 'owed; question' is work owed. (O2) Withheld wins over conditional: where the work order says 'every result is withheld' (a recorded special district, a recorded split lot, a column that was not read) every result is withheld, a user's statement included. Conditions add up: a shown value carries every condition that applies to it. (O3) A result computed from a withheld result is withheld and names it; a result computed from a conditional result carries its conditions. (O4) The recorded lot area with no outline area to compare it with: results that need the area are conditional on the recorded figure, saying that it could not be compared (never settled). No recorded area: withheld; the outline's area is never used in its place. The tolerance of the comparison is not this task's: agreement is an input. (O5) Gap K9: on a lot with a recorded overlay a residential result may be shown only where an independent reading of the overlay text supports it, and a legal reading is never the subject of a conditional result. WHICH results the merged readings support is NOT decided in this module and it holds no table of them: for each result the caller says 'an independent reading supports showing this result under this overlay' or 'no reading supports it yet' (with the sections whose reading is owed). Supported: the result is decided as for a lot without an overlay. Not supported: WITHHELD as work owed, naming the reading that is owed, together with everything computed from it. A recorded overlay with no statement of support at all: every residential result withheld. (The other task of this wave is writing a new reading of the overlay text into the reference cases; which results that reading supports is settled, with a test tied to the merged rows, by the piece that wires this module in.) (O6) One of the four conditions without a data source recorded as PRESENT: every zoning result is withheld (the work order says which results each can change is not established). (O7) An inclusionary housing area, a flood zone or a landmark 'not read': the results the work order says it can change are withheld as missing information (a column that was not read is never taken as 'none'). (O8) Gap K3 is applied as the work order states it (coverage withheld for a lot of 30,000 sq ft or more), although the merged step-P3 reading suggests that the different maximum does not reach R6B; the report says so and changes nothing. (O9) The two legal measures used to compare the reach (100 feet; 135 degrees) are taken from the captured ZR 12-10 definition of a corner lot and ZR 23-344, each with its capture id beside it and the comparison written as the captured words have it. (O10) Any combination that neither the work order nor these readings decide is WITHHELD as work owed and is listed in the report as an open question. Nothing is guessed. TESTS take their expected outcomes from outside the module: from the sentences of the work order's sections 5 and 6 and of its tests H2, H3, H4, H5, H6, H9 and H11, each quoted beside the test that uses it, at the level of 'which way does each result appear'; whether a result is settled or conditional follows from the case the test builds (the conditions it supplies as checked and absent, a user's statement, two figures that disagree). The lots' measurements are read from the reach rows of the corner-reach reference case through the loader. To keep the two pieces of this wave independent, the tests read NO other reference row (the other task may supersede rows while this one is built); the reviewers compare the outcomes with the merged rows by hand. No reason text contains the phrase of gap K7. NOT IN THIS TASK: any edit to an existing file; calling the module; emitting anything; any zoning number; any rule file, register entry, schema, fixture, screen or drawing.
business_reason: Part 0 of the work order makes the result honest. Cutting the engine work in two keeps each piece reviewable: this piece holds the whole question of how a result may appear, in new files that change nothing, so it can be checked line by line against the work order and the reference cases before the second piece wires it into the engine and emits contract 1.3.0. The owner's rules it serves: unknown stays unknown (R229); every known gap is corrected and tested or the result shows 'not known' (R237); no whole-lot 100 percent coverage until the geometry supports it (R238); missing inputs stay unanswered (R240); a user's assumption supports only a labelled conditional result (R255); conflicting areas are never chosen between automatically (R257); missing information and unfinished work are different (R258); 'not checked' is not 'confirmed' and a district's height limit is not the property's confirmed maximum (R267, R268, R269).

risks: A decision that shows more than the work order allows (a result settled by silence; a district's limit shown as the property's) -> S1, S6 and the reviewers' line-by-line check of the decision table against section 5
A point the work order leaves open filled in silently -> the readings O1 to O10 are named in the packet; O10 withholds everything else and lists it
A table of what a reading supports hidden in the module and going stale when a new reading is merged -> reading O5 and S8: the module holds none; the caller states it
Expected outcomes taken from the module itself -> the tests read the reference rows and the work order's cases; the QA reviewer checks where each comes from
A legal number inside the module -> S9; the only legal measures are the two of reading O9, each with its capture id
